change: RudderStack blog and homepage now lead with 'customer context for AI' aimed at data teams.
whyItMatters: Pulls the warehouse-native conversation toward AI infrastructure. Data buyers may start comparing us on AI readiness instead of activation.
whatToSay: "Great, your context is in the warehouse. Who acts on it? Let's look at how your marketers get from that context to a live campaign."

change: Two closed-lost notes this month cite Data 360 being bundled into an existing Salesforce renewal.
whyItMatters: We're losing these deals at procurement. Reps need to find out about the bundle earlier and build the cost-of-ownership case before the renewal date.
whatToSay: "When is your Salesforce renewal? Let's list what a bundled CDP still needs from your data team before that date, so you can decide on capability with time to spare."

change: mParticle added three commerce media integrations that connect into the Rokt network.
whyItMatters: Points to a bigger push into ecommerce and retail media. Relevant for retail prospects only, for now.
whatToSay: No talk track yet. Watch for it in retail deals.

change: mParticle launched on-device audience evaluation for mobile apps.
whyItMatters: App-first prospects will ask whether audiences can update in-session. Product should confirm our answer and whether it's a gap.
whatToSay: "Which in-app moments actually need sub-second audiences, and which run fine on warehouse freshness? Let's size that before it drives the decision."

change: Segment homepage headline shifted from 'customer data platform' language to 'customer AI' language.
whyItMatters: Packaged CDPs are reframing around AI. Our comparison pages still argue the old CDP category, so we risk sounding a step behind.
whatToSay: "AI can only use the data it can see. Where does your full customer model live today, and does the AI get all of it or a copy?"

change: Adobe published comparison content aimed at composable CDP buyers that describes warehouse-native as a DIY project.
whyItMatters: Directly targets our category with a 'build vs. buy' frame. Enterprise execs will repeat it in deals, so we need a crisp counter on our own comparison page.
whatToSay: "Composable means you use your data where it already lives, with no copy into another platform. Which of your teams owns the model your campaigns run on?"

change: Long implementation timelines are a recurring theme across public reviews of packaged CDPs this quarter (summarized theme, not a single review).
whyItMatters: Time to value is a proof point we should lead with, backed by our own implementation data. CS can also use it at renewals.
whatToSay: "What's your target date for the first live audience? Let's work back from that and compare what each option needs before day one."

change: Segment mentions in mid-market discovery calls rose for the third straight week (Gong tracker).
whyItMatters: Segment is showing up earlier in mid-market cycles, usually because it's already installed. Reps need the 'keep Segment, add Hightouch' play ready.
whatToSay: "Keep Segment for collection if it's working. Where do your audiences get built today, and who owns them?"

change: Segment launched a no-code audience builder aimed at marketers, working on warehouse-linked data.
whyItMatters: Weakens our 'marketers can self-serve on warehouse data' differentiator in mid-market deals where Segment is already installed.
whatToSay: "Ask how audiences stay in sync with the warehouse when the data team changes the model. Who gets paged when a column is renamed?"

change: Salesforce moved identity resolution from an add-on into the base Data 360 edition.
whyItMatters: Removes a line item we used in cost conversations. Execs will hear 'it's included now' and treat Data 360 as the default for Salesforce shops.
whatToSay: "Included is good. Ask which data it resolves: only what's been copied into Data 360, or everything in your warehouse?"

change: RudderStack posted 8 new Account Executive roles focused on EMEA enterprise.
whyItMatters: Suggests an EMEA enterprise push in the next two quarters. Useful for EMEA territory planning. Reps don't need it yet.
whatToSay: No talk track. FYI for EMEA sales leadership.

change: Braze AI Decisioning Studio added goal-based agent setup for lifecycle marketers.
whyItMatters: Overlaps with our AI Decisioning pitch for Braze customers. Braze is also a partner, so the line should be 'better together.'
whatToSay: "Braze is great at delivering the message. Our agents decide using everything in your warehouse, then hand off to Braze to send."

change: Adobe announced an expanded zero-copy connector with a major cloud data warehouse.
whyItMatters: Adobe can now claim 'warehouse access' in enterprise deals. We need the difference between querying the warehouse and running on it to be clear.
whatToSay: "Ask which features work on warehouse data directly and which still need the data loaded into Adobe first."
